problem_type: Windows process teardown returns unobserved success
symptom: The shared script tree terminator returns true when taskkill is missing or fails.
class_root: Shared script teardown admission confuses attempting cleanup with proof of success.
affected_population: Windows taskkill unavailable/nonzero and already-exited children
internal_only_reason: Existing Node child-process owner and isolated native fixtures; no model or external API.
invariants: A failed native tree termination cannot return success.
An already-observed exited child can return false, but an unproved live child fails closed.
POSIX process-group ownership and test-double signal semantics remain unchanged.

door_reduction.why_not: The independent delivery, headless client, radar and validation callers retain their tasks; one existing tree owner enforces native result evidence for all.

generality_proof: The shared owner checks both spawn failure and unsuccessful exit across every Windows caller, without tool/provider-specific exceptions.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Generated scripts door map; native CLI bridge now passes this existing shared owner to each selected runner.

prevention.invariant: Unproved tree cleanup never reports true.
prevention.failure_mode: Throw process_cleanup_failed for an unobserved live child; observed exit returns false.
prevention.strategy: Check native command result before reporting completion.

legacy_paths.rationale: Unconditional Windows success is removed in the same change.

dependency_lifecycle.current: Supported Windows taskkill and Node child_process
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Retain current platform owner; no replacement process engine.
exit_criteria: Revisit on supported platform changes; native failure and descendant fixtures must remain green.

migration: No user processes or configuration changed; tests own all children.
residual_risks: POSIX native process-group acceptance is unavailable on this Windows host.
